label: November 30–December 06
title: “He Delighteth in Mercy” —  Micah; Nahum; Habakkuk; Zephan

items.text: Old Testament prophets reveal how we can turn away from pride and wickedness. They were not just prophets of doom, but prophets of deliverance, tempering descriptions of destruction with invitations to come unto Christ and receive His forgiveness. This was the Lord’s way anciently, and it is His way today; His ways are everlasting.

Micah invites us to consider what the Lord requires of us. He asks us to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God. These principles are paramount as the Lord evaluates our lives, guiding us toward righteous living and a closer relationship with Him.

The Lord is a strong hold in the day of trouble. Nahum's ministry foretold destruction but also spoke of God's mercy and goodness. It is important to understand both His wrath and His love, recognizing His power to deliver and His willingness to forgive those who turn to Him.

Even prophets sometimes grapple with questions about the Lord’s ways and His timing. Habakkuk’s honest inquiries reveal that it is natural to seek understanding. The Lord’s response assures us that His plans unfold in His own time, inviting us to trust in His divine will.

When faced with unanswered questions or seemingly unfair circumstances, we are inspired by Habakkuk’s example to trust the Lord. His prayer of praise and faith in chapter 3 demonstrates a profound reliance on God, even amidst hardship, teaching us to seek His strength.

Habakkuk teaches us to rejoice in the Lord, even when temporal blessings are absent. By focusing on spiritual blessings and developing greater faith, we can learn to find joy and peace in God’s provisions, regardless of our earthly circumstances. His strength sustains us.

Spiritual insights take time and cannot be forced. The Lord counseled Habakkuk to be patient, saying, “Wait for it; because it will surely come.” This teaches us the importance of patient anticipation and enduring faith as we seek answers and divine guidance.

The Lord does not delight in condemning us; rather, “he delighteth in mercy.” This eternal principle remains true today. While judgments may be necessary, His ultimate desire is for us to repent and receive His boundless mercy through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.

The Lord is good and provides a strong refuge in times of trouble. Nahum’s message, though foretelling destruction, ultimately points to God’s unwavering goodness. We can find solace and safety in Him, knowing He is our constant support and protector.

Even when the wicked seem to prevail, we can trust the Lord’s ultimate justice and timing. Habakkuk’s wrestling with this truth is a reminder that our perspective is limited, but God’s vision is perfect and His purposes will be fulfilled.
